reuse.why: Most consumers reuse getScheduledAmount, but the API independently resolves amounts and the shared helper reimplements getApproxNumberThreshold.

duplication.why: The change removes several local calculations but retains a separate API amount resolver and duplicates the existing tolerance calculation.

placement.why: The shared schedules module appropriately owns expected-amount policy, but the API serializer also embeds that policy instead of delegating.

scope.why: The edits are focused on expected schedule amounts, their consumers, API types, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Centralizing most consumers improves maintenance, but independent API policy and duplicated tolerance arithmetic leave multiple definitions to update.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts: scheduleModel.toExternal bypasses getScheduledAmount; packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getScheduledAmount bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: scheduleModel.toExternal reshapes the shared amount resolver into nested ternaries with reordered numeric, missing, and range dispatch.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains the optional op parameter and an isapprox branch, while scheduleModel.toExternal maintains an independent amount-resolution path.
